Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract and rollout evidence, then use the wake-visual inspection skill before the fish-control bookshelf transfer. I’ll keep the implementation to exactly one candidate and will not consider it done until both required notes files are updated.

The inherited guidance shows this is no longer the naive-seed stage: the lineage already has repeatable captures and several mechanism-isolating comparisons. I’m now comparing the sampled captured variants closely, including initialization, trajectory, load, saturation, and both visual rows, so the next change targets a real remaining weakness rather than retuning the carrier.

Both sampled sheets confirm direct uniform still water and the same physical picture: self-propelled motion with a coherent, alternating reverse-vortex street, a smooth target-signed arc, no visible wake collapse, and capture. There is no multimodal failure rollout in the sampled set; the only weaker comparator is the slightly slower v32 capture, while the inherited scalar log supplies the catastrophic opposite-sign rate-projection failure. The three v33 artifacts are code-equivalent apart from comments/version and produce byte-identical visual evidence, which makes their inactive mechanism itself useful evidence.

The bookshelf protocol now applies because I’ve anchored the transfer to those observations. I’m consulting its mechanism references before proposing the candidate architecture.

The candidate hypothesis is now fixed. I’ll retain the assigned v32 carrier, whole-wave projection, and proven head-to-tail steering recovery, and add one bounded mechanism: target-signed curvature only while the de-gaited body-frame bearing is outside its centerline band and still diverging; it releases automatically when bearing contracts and fades on approach. This is a response-gated redirect, not a gain sweep or a new oscillator.

The shelf contribution is the C-start/closed-loop-CPG invariant—strengthen curvature when observed geometry is worsening, then release on observed recovery. Species kinematics, published gains, exact phases, and routes are not being transferred. I’m recording that provenance and falsification before touching the policy, as required by the visual-inspection skill.

The frozen-state replay confirms the new term is genuinely active and bounded: it changes commands on 46% of recorded states, is always opposite the diverging bearing sign, averages only `0.129` in route-request units, and changes either joint by at most `1.41 rad/T²` while preserving the `31.416 rad/T²` physical cap. Its strongest intervention is in the evidenced `8–12 T` sweep, not in the carrier definition.

I’m now converting the repeated v33 result into the durable negative lesson: bidirectional rejected-steering recovery is not additive on this route, despite its tiny score change, so later workers should stop reproducing comment-distinct versions of that same inactive topology.

The candidate, provenance notes, and durable lesson are all updated. I’m invoking the workspace’s prescribed lightweight check runner now; it will check semantic guidance change, the policy contract and parameter schema, and file boundaries without running CFD.

The configured check-runner agent could not start because its pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unavailable in this account environment. I’ve still invoked it as required; I’ll now execute its three exact non-CFD checks directly and repair anything they flag.

The first check exposed a workspace-metadata defect, not a policy defect: the rendered README marks the same optimizer parent as “copied to guidance/” twice, so the checker cannot uniquely resolve the parent. I’m removing only the duplicated marker line, then rerunning the check against the unchanged parent artifact.

All three prescribed checks now pass: the semantic guidance/notes check, the Julia policy contract check, and the solver boundary check. No CFD was run. I’m doing the final artifact audit now—non-empty candidate, material diffs from the assigned parent, and exact locations for handoff.

Implemented exactly one v34 target-policy candidate with bounded bearing-divergence recovery while preserving the proven carrier and steering structure.

- Candidate: [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:11)
- Evidence, bookshelf transfer, hypothesis, and replay: [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1)
- Reusable negative lesson on non-additive v33 allocation: [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:115)

All prescribed non-CFD checks pass: guidance semantics, Julia policy contract/schema, and solver boundary. The configured check-runner model was unavailable, so its exact commands were executed directly. No formal CFD was run; EvE will evaluate the candidate after exit.
